Imagine you have a circular piece of plywood. You randomly hammer 6 nails into the very edge of the circle. If you wrap a rubber band around those nails, what are the odds that the center of the wood is trapped inside that rubber band?

This is a pretty classic problem in the field of geometric probability. The idea was inspired by a video I saw online, but a detailed write-up can also be found at [Brainstellar](https://brainstellar.com/puzzles/211) (along with some other really interesting puzzles!)

## Interactive Simulation

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import { createInteractiveCircle } from "./visualization.js"

app = {
  // layout setup
  const container = html`<div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center;">
    <div class="controls-container">
       <div id="slider-container"></div>
       <button class="randomize-btn">Randomize Positions</button>
    </div>
    <div id="canvas-container"></div>
  </div>`;

  const sliderContainer = container.querySelector("#slider-container");
  const canvasContainer = container.querySelector("#canvas-container");
  const randBtn = container.querySelector("button");

  let currentLogic = null; 
  
  function updateCanvas(n, mode) {
    canvasContainer.innerHTML = "";
    const c = DOM.canvas(400, 400);
    canvasContainer.appendChild(c);
    
    currentLogic = createInteractiveCircle(c, n, mode);
  }

  // slider
  const sliderWrapper = Inputs.range([3, 12], {value: 6, step: 1, label: "Points (n)"});
  sliderContainer.appendChild(sliderWrapper);

  const rangeInput = sliderWrapper.querySelector("input");

  // slider change
  rangeInput.addEventListener("input", () => {
    updateCanvas(rangeInput.valueAsNumber, "even");
  });

  // button click
  randBtn.onclick = () => {
    if (currentLogic) {
      currentLogic.randomize();
    }
  };

  updateCanvas(6, "even");

  return container;
}
```

## The Mathematical Derivation

Instead of calculating the probability of the center being *inside*, we calculate the probability of the **complement**: the center being **outside**.

### 1. The Semicircle Condition

The center of the circle lies outside the polygon if and only if all points lie within the same arc (a semicircle).

### 2. Fixing a Boundary

## Results

| Points | Probability |
|--------|-------------|
| 3      | 25.0%       |
| 4      | 37.5%       |
| 5      | 50.0%       |
| 6      | 62.5%       |
| 10     | 87.9%       |

As $n \to \infty$, the probability approaches 1.

## Conclusion

This problem beautifully demonstrates how geometric intuition connects to discrete probability. The interactive visualization above lets you explore different values of $n$ and see the pattern emerge.
